items.bold: 16 ships traversed Hormuz Monday — not zero, but barely 10% of pre-war levels.
items.text: CNN (MarineTraffic data, Monday): 16 ships traversed Hormuz — nine entered including two Iranian-flagged vessels, seven exited including one Iranian cargo ship. Very low vs 130-160 pre-war, but not the zero of Sunday. Iran parliament's construction committee head Rezaei-Kouchi (April 19): parliament planning a law making hostile-country ships unable to pass and all others needing to pay tolls and coordinate with Iranian authorities. This signals Iran is trying to legally institutionalise control of Hormuz as leverage in any deal — not just use it as a temporary weapon. Araghchi told Lavrov: Hormuz "insecurity is the result of the military aggression of the United States and Zionist regime." Iran will "take appropriate decisions to safeguard its national interests."

items.bold: THIRD US CARRIER converging. USS Abraham Lincoln + Ford + George HW Bush = unprecedented naval force.
items.text: NBC News (live blog) confirmed the full US naval order of battle: USS Abraham Lincoln Carrier Strike Group in the Gulf of Oman near Hormuz (supporting blockade). USS Gerald R. Ford CSG in the northern Red Sea (deployed ~300 days — one of longest in history). USS George HW Bush near Madagascar, heading north through the Indian Ocean — traveled all the way around Africa to avoid the Bab al-Mandab Strait (Houthi threat). The Bush is expected to relieve the Ford soon, creating a temporary overlap of three carrier battle groups in the region. This is the largest concentration of US naval power in the region since at least Gulf War. It serves both as blockade enforcement and pre-positioning for resumed strikes.

items.bold: CHINA's Xi pressed Saudi MBS for Hormuz reopening. Egypt mediating alongside Pakistan.
items.text: CNN (Monday live blog): China's Xi Jinping warned that the Strait of Hormuz "must be fully open for vessels" in his most explicit comments on the choked waterway — made during a phone call with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi had separately told Araghchi: "working to resume normal passage of the strait is a unanimous call from the international community." China sources 20% of its oil from Iran, and more than half its overall energy via Hormuz — maximum pressure on Iran from its closest partner. Egypt is also actively working to bring the US and Iran back to negotiations, in coordination with Pakistan (CNN, sourced from regional official).

items.bold: HEZBOLLAH broke Lebanon ceasefire — detonated bombs, killed 4 Israeli tanks. Lebanon fraying.
items.text: Hezbollah confirmed Monday it detonated explosives in south Lebanon in an attack against Israeli forces in Deir Siryan, destroying four tanks in a convoy of eight — the first claimed Hezbollah attack since the 10-day Lebanon ceasefire went into effect last Thursday. This is significant because: (1) Iran has repeatedly said Hormuz closure is linked to Lebanon ceasefire; (2) a Lebanon ceasefire collapse could give Iran justification to escalate Hormuz beyond its current posture; (3) it undermines the ceasefire framework that enabled Iran's brief Hormuz opening. Israeli-Lebanese ambassadors are scheduled to meet in Washington DC Tuesday to discuss a pause in military activity. Hezbollah's Naim Qassem reportedly urged Lebanon to cancel this meeting, calling it "pointless."

military.t: THIRD US CARRIER CONVERGING — USS Bush Near Madagascar. Three CSGs: Lincoln, Ford, Bush.
military.d: NBC News confirmed the full US naval order of battle: USS Abraham Lincoln CSG in Gulf of Oman near Hormuz (supporting blockade). USS Gerald R. Ford CSG in northern Red Sea (~300 days deployed — one of longest deployments in history). USS George HW Bush departing near Madagascar heading north through Indian Ocean — traveled around Africa to avoid Houthi Bab al-Mandab threat. Bush expected to relieve Ford, creating temporary overlap of three carrier battle groups. This is the largest US naval force concentration in the Gulf region since the Gulf War. It signals: (1) full blockade capability, (2) pre-positioning for resumed strikes, (3) maximum pressure ahead of tonight's deadline. For India: this naval posture will remain even if a ceasefire extension is announced — it's a permanent feature of any deal framework.

military.t: China's Xi Pressed Saudi MBS for Hormuz Reopening — Most Explicit Beijing Call Yet.
military.d: CNN (Monday live blog): China's President Xi Jinping warned Saudi Crown Prince MBS directly that the Strait of Hormuz "must be fully open for vessels" — his most explicit call since the war began. China sources 20% of its oil from Iran and more than half its energy via Hormuz — Xi is under domestic pressure to resolve this. Beijing also condemned the "forced interception" of the Touska. China's Wang Yi had separately told Araghchi: "resuming normal passage is a unanimous call from the international community." This dual-track Chinese pressure — on Saudi Arabia AND on Iran — is significant: it signals Beijing is actively pushing Iran to reach a deal. Egypt is also mediating alongside Pakistan (CNN, regional official). Egypt-Pakistan-Turkey-China pressure all pointing toward Iran attending talks.

military.t: Iran Parliament Legislating Permanent Hormuz Toll System — Institutionalising Control.
military.d: Wikipedia Hormuz crisis page (confirmed April 19): Iranian parliament's construction committee head Mohammad Rezaei-Kouchi said parliament was planning to pass a law making boats from "hostile" countries unable to pass the Strait, while all others would need to pay tolls and coordinate with Iranian authorities. This signals Iran's strategic intent: rather than using Hormuz as a temporary war weapon, Tehran wants to permanently institutionalise sovereign control — including toll collection — as a fait accompli in any deal. This is a maximalist position that goes far beyond what the US, UAE, Saudi Arabia, or international shipping law will accept. It explains why the nuclear issue has been described as solvable compared to the Hormuz sovereignty question.

military.t: Key Intelligence: Iran FM Araghchi Told Lavrov "Appropriate Decisions" Coming. Trump Approval at New Low.
military.d: Iran FM Araghchi told Russian FM Lavrov Monday: Iran "will take appropriate decisions to safeguard its national interests and security" regarding Hormuz — deliberately ambiguous. Could mean deal OR escalation. Russia separately: Lavrov told Araghchi Moscow "remains ready to help find solutions." NBC poll released Monday: Trump's approval rating hit a new low — 63% disapprove of his performance. This matters because domestic political pressure may accelerate Trump's desire to end the war quickly — possibly accepting less than his stated maximalist demands. Trump already showed flexibility when Rubio conceded Iran can have a civilian nuclear program. Vance told Fox News: "There really is, I think, a grand deal to be had here, but it's up to the Iranians to take the next step." Both sides still say a deal is possible.

assessment.body:
Tuesday April 21. Ceasefire expires in 18 hours. This is what we know at 7:30 AM IST.

THE IRAN REVERSAL — MOST IMPORTANT SIGNAL
• NYT (two senior Iranian officials): Iran delegation "making plans to head to Islamabad on Tuesday"
• Iran FM Araghchi to Pakistan FM Dar: "taking all aspects into consideration, will decide"
• CNN: Vance CONFIRMED attending — Witkoff and Kushner also going
• Trump to New York Post: "We're supposed to have the talks. Nobody's playing games."
• Pakistan deploying 10,000 security, US C-17 at Nur Khan, Serena Hotel locked down
• Classic Iran pattern: refuse publicly → reverse at last minute → show up

THE DEADLINE
• Ceasefire expires: 0000 GMT Wednesday = 8 PM ET Tuesday = 1:30 AM IST Wednesday
• India market Tuesday (today): 9:15 AM to 3:30 PM — under the ceasefire
• India market Wednesday: 9:15 AM — potentially first session after lapse
• If talks show progress by tonight ET: informal extension possible
• If Iran doesn't attend: war resumes, Wednesday 9:15 AM India open under fire

THE THREAT
• Ghalibaf: "Over past 2 weeks we have prepared to reveal new cards on the battlefield"
• IRGC confirmed rearming faster than pre-war pace
• Hezbollah detonated bombs Monday — 4 Israeli tanks destroyed — first Lebanon ceasefire breach
• Iran parliament legislating permanent Hormuz toll system
• Third US carrier (USS Bush) converging from Madagascar — three CSGs in theatre
• This is the most militarised standoff since Feb 28

THE PRESSURE ON IRAN TO ATTEND
• China's Xi personally pressed Saudi MBS for Hormuz opening — Beijing telling Tehran
• Egypt actively mediating alongside Pakistan
• Turkey, Egypt, Pakistan all pushing Iran back to table
• Iran's economy: $140M daily oil revenue zeroed by US blockade
• 25 ships turned back, Touska seized — blockade working
• Iran "will take appropriate decisions" — Araghchi to Lavrov — still ambiguous

INDIA's SPECIFIC POSITION
• Markets open in ~2 hours at 9:15 AM IST
• Sensex 78,520 (prev close). Nifty 24,365. VIX 19.01
• Expected VIX at open: 20-23 (elevated uncertainty)
• Brent $95-96 = petrol/diesel hike pressure, LPG cut reversed
• Rupee ~94.00-94.50 — weakening but not panicking
• Wednesday: ceasefire expiry + Infosys Q4 results — highest-stakes dual event of the war
• 280 Indian seafarers affected. Multiple Indian ships attacked. Op Urja Suraksha HIGH ALERT

THE 40-40-20 CALL
• 40%: Iran attends Islamabad today, framework agreed, informal extension → Sensex 79,000-81,000+, Brent $84-90
• 40%: Iran no-shows, ceasefire lapses 1:30 AM IST Wed, Ghalibaf reveals battlefield cards → Sensex 72,000-75,000, Brent $108-120, rupee 97+
• 20%: De-facto standoff, both sides hold fire without formal extension → Sensex 75,000-78,000, Brent $96-102

VERDICT: The single question that determines everything: does the Iranian delegation board a flight to Islamabad today? If yes: 18 hours of diplomacy, probable informal extension, markets hold. If no: the most destructive phase of this war begins on Wednesday morning. India will feel it immediately.
